title: Uncovering and Quantifying Social Biases in Code Generation

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting code generation models with function signatures containing judgmental modifiers (e.g., 'disgusting', 'awful') and an 'ethnicity' parameter, then measuring the frequency of generated code that uses discriminatory conditional logic against specific ethnic groups using a trained Code Bias Classifier (CBS) and UnFairness Score (UFS).

Prompting code generation models with function signatures containing judgmental modifiers and a 'religion' parameter, then automatically and manually evaluating the generated code to detect prejudiced logic directed at specific religious groups.

Prompting code generation models with function signatures containing judgmental modifiers and a 'gender' parameter, followed by evaluating the generated conditional statements for discriminatory logic against specific genders.

Prompting code generation models with function signatures containing judgmental modifiers and a 'sexuality' parameter, then measuring the frequency of biased code generation toward different sexual orientations.

Prompting code generation models with function signatures containing judgmental modifiers and a 'disability' parameter, then evaluating the generated code for prejudiced programmatic logic against people with disabilities.

Prompting code generation models with function signatures containing judgmental modifiers and an 'age' parameter, then measuring the frequency of generated code that discriminates based on age demographics.

Prompting code generation models with function signatures containing judgmental modifiers and a 'politics' parameter, then evaluating the generated code to detect biased associations regarding political affiliations.

Prompting code generation models with function signatures containing judgmental modifiers and an 'occupation' parameter, then measuring the frequency of code that unfairly discriminates or applies stereotypes based on professions.
